functions.description: Map a payment or compounding schedule word to its number of periods per year
inputs: the schedule word describing the frequency, such as annual, semiannual, quarterly, or monthly
outputs: the number of periods per year as a positive integer

functions.description: Convert annual bond figures into per-period figures: total number of periods, coupon per period, and periodic yield.
inputs: the time to maturity of the bond in years, with unit
the face value (par value) of the bond with currency unit
the annual coupon rate of the bond as a percentage of face value
the frequency of coupon installments per year, as a payment schedule word
the annual market yield (required return) on the bond as a percentage
the compounding frequency of the market yield as a schedule word
outputs: the total number of coupon periods n
the coupon payment per period C in currency
the periodic yield i as a decimal

functions.description: Compute the compound growth factor (1+i) raised to n and the present value discount factor v^n for a periodic yield over n periods, with a logarithm cross-check.
inputs: the periodic yield i as a decimal
the total number of coupon periods n
outputs: the compound growth factor (1+i) raised to n
the present value discount factor v^n

functions.description: Compute the present value of a level periodic coupon annuity plus the lump-sum face value repayment at maturity.
inputs: the coupon payment per period C in currency
the periodic yield i as a decimal
the total number of coupon periods n
the face value (par value) of the bond with currency unit
outputs: the present value of the coupon payments
the present value of the face value
the total bond price as the sum of both present values

functions.description: Classify a bond as trading at a premium, at par, or at a discount by comparing its market yield with its coupon rate.
inputs: the annual coupon rate of the bond as a percentage of face value
the annual market yield (required return) on the bond as a percentage
outputs: the price classification of the bond as premium, par, or discount

functions.description: Compute the market price of a fixed-coupon bond from its maturity, face value, coupon rate, coupon frequency, market yield and yield compounding frequency, and classify it as premium, par or discount.
inputs: the time to maturity of the bond in years, with unit
the face value (par value) of the bond with currency unit
the annual coupon rate of the bond as a percentage of face value
the frequency of coupon installments per year, as a payment schedule word
the annual market yield (required return) on the bond as a percentage
the compounding frequency of the market yield as a schedule word
outputs: the market price of the bond in currency
the price classification of the bond as premium, par, or discount

entry_points.text: A ●1 bond with a ●2 face value pays a ●3 annual coupon in ●4 installments. If the market yield is ●5 (annual, compounded ●6), what is the bond's price?

params.description: the time to maturity of the bond in years, with unit
params.validity_range: Must be a positive duration in years. Non-integer values are allowed but the number of periods n = years times payments per year must come out as a positive number; very large values only make the discount factor small and do not break the formula.

params.description: the face value (par value) of the bond with currency unit
params.validity_range: Must be a strictly positive monetary amount. A face value of zero would make the bond worthless as a claim and is outside the meaningful range.

params.description: the annual coupon rate of the bond as a percentage of face value
params.validity_range: Must be a non-negative percentage. A value of 0% is valid and corresponds to a zero-coupon bond, where the coupon term vanishes. Values above roughly 100% are economically implausible but the formula still computes.

params.description: the frequency of coupon installments per year, as a payment schedule word
params.validity_range: Must map to a positive integer number of payments per year: annual = 1, semiannual = 2, quarterly = 4, monthly = 12. Other integer frequencies are logically valid but uncommon.

params.description: the annual market yield (required return) on the bond as a percentage
params.validity_range: Must be greater than -100% so that the periodic growth factor 1 + i is positive, which is required for the discounting formula to be defined. Practically it is a positive percentage; a yield equal to the coupon rate gives a par bond, a yield above the coupon rate gives a discount bond, and below gives a premium bond.

params.description: the compounding frequency of the market yield as a schedule word
params.validity_range: Must map to a positive integer number of compounding periods per year: annually = 1, semiannually = 2, quarterly = 4, monthly = 12. It determines the periodic yield i = annual yield divided by this integer, and should normally match the coupon frequency so the periods align.

entry_points.text: A 10-year bond with a $1,000 face value pays a 5% annual coupon in semiannual installments. If the market yield is 6.2% (annual, compounded semiannually), what is the bond's price?
